topics.name: Kinds of sentences: statement, question, command, exclamation

options: How a mess this street is!
What a mess this streets is!
What a mess this street is!
questions.rule: Use What a + noun in an exclamation, and end it with !. 'How' goes with an adjective alone.

options: Where did all this litter come from?
Where did all this litter came from?
Where all this litter did come from?
questions.rule: After did, use the base form: did ... come. The order is Where + did + subject + verb.

options: I will gets some ice at once.
I will get some ice at once.
I will got some ice at once.
questions.rule: After will, always use the base form of the verb: will get.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A command or request uses the base form of the verb: please throw.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: will is always followed by the base form: will help, never 'will helps'.
Use What a + noun in an exclamation: What a terrible mess! ('How' goes with an adjective alone.)

questions.after: is the newspaper so late today?
questions.rule: To ask for a reason, use Why.
A negative command begins with Do not + base verb. Please makes it polite.

options: I will fetch her at once.
I will fetched her at once.
questions.rule: To offer to do something now, say I will + base verb: I will fetch.

chat: I saw an old tyre in the middle of the road!
questions.rule: Question order: When + did + you + base verb: When did you see it?
Commands use the base form of every verb: Run and fetch.

options: Who are responsible for this mess is?
Who is responsible for this mess?
questions.rule: A wh- question needs a verb in the right place: Who is responsible ...?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After do or does in a question, use the base form: do the birds build?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A negative command is Do not + base verb: Do not dump.

questions.before: If we sort the litter, the Mayor
questions.rule: For a future action, use will + base verb: will arrange.

questions.after: the door; it is cold outside.
questions.rule: A request with please uses the base form of the verb: please shut.
When What is the subject, no 'did' is needed: What happened?
Future: subject + will + base verb + object: I will dress the wound.
News is uncountable: no 'a' and no plural. Say What great news!

options: Let me opens the door for you.
Let me to open the door for you.
Let me open the door for you.
questions.rule: After Let me, use the base form with no 'to': Let me open.

options: Did you saw the rubbish on the road?
Did you see the rubbish on the road?
Saw you the rubbish on the road?
questions.rule: A yes/no question in the past: Did + subject + base verb (see) + ?

options: How all this rubbish did gather here overnight?
How did all this rubbish gather here overnight?
How did all this rubbish gathered here overnight?
questions.rule: Question order: How + did + subject + base verb: How did all this rubbish gather?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: An exclamation with an adjective alone starts with How: How clean our street looks!

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Next week is the future: will + base verb = will collect.

questions.after: of these bins is for plastic waste?
questions.rule: To choose from a group (of these bins), use Which.
Let's (let us) is followed by the base form of the verb: Let's clean.
Exclamation pattern: What a + adjective + noun + subject + verb + !
Question order: Where + can + we + verb ...?

chat: Will you come to the cleanliness drive on Sunday?
options: Yes, I will bring two big bags for the litter.
Yes, I will brought two big bags for the litter.
Yes, I will brings two big bags for the litter.
questions.rule: Answer a will question with will + base verb: I will bring.

chat: Your school bus is late again.
options: Why the bus is late today?
Why is the bus late today?
Why does the bus late today?
questions.rule: In a question, is comes before the subject: Why is the bus late?
After to, use the object pronoun her. A command uses the base verb Give.

options: The doctor will dress the wound in a hour.
The doctor will dresses the wound in an hour.
The doctor will dress the wound in an hour.
questions.rule: will + base verb (dress). Use an before a vowel sound: an hour (the h is silent).

options: Where was the animals hiding all this time?
Where were the animals hide all this time?
Where were the animals hiding all this time?
questions.rule: Animals is plural, so use were, and were + -ing: were ... hiding.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After the verb gave, use object pronouns: gave Madhu and her.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Child has an irregular plural: children. There is no 'childs'.
After the verb give, use an object pronoun: give us.

questions.after: your sisters when the milkman came?
questions.rule: Sisters is plural and the time is past (came), so use were.
A request: Please + base verb + object + place word.

chat: When will the garbage van come?
options: It will come on eight o'clock.
It will comes at eight o'clock.
It will come at eight o'clock.
questions.rule: Use at with clock times, and will + base verb: will come.

chat: Look, I fixed my broken bicycle myself!
options: What a clever boy you are!
How a clever boy you are!
questions.rule: With a singular noun, the exclamation starts What a: What a clever boy you are!

options: Did nobody saw who brought the garbage here?
Did nobody see who brought the garbage here?
Did nobody see who bring the garbage here?
questions.rule: After Did, use the base verb see; the past action inside uses the past form brought.

options: Why doesn't you all dispose of the garbage properly?
Why don't you all dispose of the garbage properly?
Why don't you all disposing of the garbage properly?
questions.rule: You takes don't, and don't + base verb: dispose.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: will is always followed by the base form: I will send.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: With does in a question, the main verb takes the base form: does your family use?

questions.after: bicycle had punctured tyres, the milkman's or the newspaper boy's?
questions.rule: To ask about the owner, use Whose. 'Who's' means 'who is'.

questions.after: we all suffer because of the poisons in the water!
questions.rule: An exclamation about how much something happens starts with How + subject + verb.
Question order: How + can + we + verb + object + place.
A negative suggestion is Let's not + base verb: Let's not pollute.

chat: What will you do with your old notebooks?
options: I will give them to my younger cousin.
I will gave them to my younger cousin.
I will give they to my younger cousin.
questions.rule: will + base verb (give). After a verb, use the object pronoun them.

chat: Beta, could you carry this bag for me?
options: Of course, aunty. Gives it to me.
Of course, aunty. Give it to I.
Of course, aunty. Give it to me.
questions.rule: A command uses the base verb Give. After to, use the object pronoun me.
